question: True or false: in the first randomised trial of phage therapy for infected burns, the viruses did worse than the standard cream?
answer: True. PhagoBurn, in French and Belgian burn units, assigned 27 patients to a cocktail of 12 viruses that kill Pseudomonas or to silver sulfadiazine cream. Bacteria fell more slowly under phages; the trial stopped early. The cocktail had lost most of its strength before use, so patients got a far weaker dose than planned.
move: Rescues get published; quiet failures of the same method rarely do.
ask: Which success stories do I hear while the quiet failures of the same method stay hidden?
trap: Trusting the steady stream of case reports of patients rescued by phages.
source: Jault et al., Lancet Infectious Diseases, 2019
reference: Jault et al., Efficacy and tolerability of a cocktail of bacteriophages to treat burn wounds infected by Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PhagoBurn): a randomised, controlled, double-blind phase 1/2 trial, The Lancet Infectious Diseases, 2019
